name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Urea subdued awaiting an Indian tender, ammonia up; Hormuz about 20% of pre-war traffic, not shut, so Alert unconfirmed
state: Urea trade was subdued on 2 Nov, with prices expected to stay under pressure until an Indian tender sets a benchmark, while the November Tampa ammonia contract settled at $645 a tonne, up $95 on October (Hortidaily). Hormuz disruption has restricted Middle East urea supply, with up to 600,000 tonnes reported waiting on vessels in September (Ausfert). Traffic through the strait is about 20% of pre-war levels (The National). Searches on 8 Nov found no report of urea up 60% in three months, and the route is impeded rather than shut, so the Alert is unconfirmed and Watch holds.
for_you: Farmers and food producers face higher nitrogen costs, especially for ammonia. Effects tend to reach planting decisions and food prices over the following seasons.
rubric_hit: Gulf exporters' shipments restricted by Hormuz disruption (Watch line); no 60% three-month urea rise or fully closed route confirmed for Alert

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
